chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saqr al-Sa'igh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Bassam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Dimashqi narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Lahi'a, from Abu Qubayl, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said:

On the Day of Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave the banner to a man from his companions, and he returned defeated. Then he gave it to another, who returned showing cowardice to his companions and they showing cowardice to him — he brought the banner back in defeat. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him — he will not return until Allah conquers by his hands.

When morning came, he said: Call Ali for me. It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, he has an eye ailment. He said: Call him. When he came, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spat in his eyes and said: O Allah, repel heat and cold from him. Then he gave him the banner and he advanced. He did not return to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) except with the conquest of Khaybar.

Then he said: When he drew near to al-Qamus, the enemies of Allah from the Jews came at him shooting arrows and stones. Ali (peace be upon him) charged at them until he drew near the gate. He dismounted his leg, then descended in anger to the base of the gate's threshold and wrenched it out. Then he threw it forty cubits behind his back. Ibn Umar said: We were not amazed at Allah's conquest of Khaybar at the hands of Ali (peace be upon him), but we were amazed at his uprooting the gate and throwing it forty cubits behind him. Forty men tried to carry it but could not manage it. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was informed of that and said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, forty angels aided him in it.

key_terms.الرَّايَة: the banner/flag — the military standard symbolizing leadership and command on the battlefield
key_terms.الْقَمُوص: al-Qamus — the name of the main fortress/stronghold at Khaybar
key_terms.تَفَلَ: he spat (lightly) — a symbolic healing action performed by the Prophet
key_terms.خَيْبَر: Khaybar — a fortified Jewish settlement in the Hijaz, conquered by the Muslims in 7 AH
key_terms.ذِرَاع: cubit — a unit of measurement, approximately 45-55 cm (the length of a forearm)
key_terms.رَمِدٌ: eye ailment — specifically, ophthalmia or inflammation of the eyes
key_terms.مَلَكًا: angel — a heavenly being sent by God to assist Ali

ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet gave the banner to Ali at the Battle of Khaybar?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the famous event of the Battle of Khaybar (7 AH / 628 CE), in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) gave the battle banner to Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) after two previous flag-bearers had returned defeated. The Prophet miraculously healed Ali's eye ailment by spitting in his eyes, and Ali subsequently conquered the fortress, uprooting its gate with superhuman strength — an act the Prophet attributed to the aid of forty angels. The hadith is narrated here by the Companion Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, transmitted through a chain that reaches Shaykh al-Saduq.
